label: copy-phase input "1" at recall positions 3-4
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and 99% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is the digit 1 (i.e. echoing an original 1; never on the first occurrence of a token, never in the original or delimiter phase). Only about 23% of copy-phase 1 inputs activate, though. Firing is concentrated where 1 sat at original position 2-3 (recall_idx 3-4 hold ~80% of mass; recall_idx 0-1 essentially never) and near the end of the copy (to_go 0-3). The largest activations (top examples ~0.9-1.0 of max) are short sequences (L=5-6) like "x y 1 p r <DEL> x y [1]", where the output that follows the 1 is p/f/r/o; those output tokens have the highest firing rates. More digits in the sequence also raise the rate. Rare weak activations occur on copy inputs p/f. What decides which 1-inputs fire beyond position is not captured: dev F1 is 0.58 for the recall_idx 3-4 predicate, and the broad predicate (any copy-phase 1) has mass recall 0.99 but precision 0.23.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=9: 1, p, f, o; t=8: 1, p, f; t=10: 1, p, f) and the token being output (most: p, f, 1, r, o, 2; least: b, e, v, w); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=3.
